served: HLA-B51 and Behcet's assessment (pathergy, ophthalmology review)
results: 1. observation of the jerks: rhythmic palatal movements at 2-3 Hz with bilateral acoustic clicks, louder on the right
2. effect of sleep: palatal tremor PERSISTS in sleep - characteristic of palatal tremor rather than true myoclonus
3. MRI brainstem / dentato-rubro-olivary pathway: inflammatory brainstem involvement in the Guillain-Mollaret triangle
4. HLA-B51 and Behcet's assessment (pathergy, ophthalmology review): consistent with Behcet's disease
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Symptomatic palatal tremor (palatal myoclonus) caused by an inflammatory lesion of the Guillain-Mollaret (dentato-rubro-olivary) pathway in the brainstem due to Behçet's disease.
1. Palatal tremor secondary to a demyelinating lesion (e.g. multiple sclerosis) in the Guillain-Mollaret triangle.
2. Palatal tremor secondary to a vascular brainstem lesion (stroke) in the dentato-rubro-olivary pathway.
3. Essential (idiopathic) palatal tremor.
